definition: Clustered data are observations grouped within larger units, whether in hierarchical or other nested arrangements, such as people within schools. This kind of grouping is common in social, behavioral, and biomedical research and is typically analyzed with multilevel statistical methods.

provenance.scope: Source record D055361; pinned source text

reasons: The packet does not define “clustered data” as a type of observations; it describes “The statistical manipulation of hierarchically and non-hierarchically nested data,” and mentions clustered data as an example within that context.

The definition’s claim that clustered data are “typically analyzed with multilevel statistical methods” is not explicitly stated in the packet; it mentions that “linear and nonlinear regression models are applied,” but does not use the phrase (or a direct equivalent) “multilevel statistical methods.”

The packet’s wording emphasizes analysis (“models are applied”) rather than the definition-style framing “observations grouped within larger units,” so part of the requested conceptual definition is not directly supported as written.
